<!--

I'm new to HA, I have no proper dev environment yet, so my test was quite simple: copied the new recorder code into the running core container, restarted it, and it worked, the DB schema changed, `schema_changes` updated, see the log below (it implicitly tested changes in #47026 also).

Previously I've modified my SQL schema (varchar 32->64) directly in my MariaDB, it was running for a few weeks without problems.

My config: MariaDB 10.5.8, with Aria storage engine on tmpfs (in-memory DB). I'm using MariaDB 10.5.8 with Alpine Linux 3.13 because max key length is 2000 bytes in this newer version, and `entity_id(255)` was too big for 1000 bytes hardcoded in MariaDB 10.4.17.

Testing matrix:

- [x] sqlite3 - needs to be excluded
- [x] mysql
- [x] postgresql - test failed

I made modifications:
- skip [sqlite](https://sqlite.org/lang_altertable.html), it can't handle it, we should execute it in several steps
- added special handling to make it work on: [postgresql](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/9.1/sql-altertable.html) and [mssql](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/t-sql/statements/alter-table-transact-sql?view=sql-server-ver15)
- default works for [mysql](https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.0/en/alter-table.html)/mariadb (and should work for [oracle](https://docs.oracle.com/cd/B28359_01/server.111/b28286/statements_3001.htm#i2103924))

If somebody accidentally tries to modify sqlite later, a warning will be written in the log, instead of a silent skip!

- Link to integration documentation on our website:

I don't think this has been addressed ...

Note that this is not a generic issue but the default release also generates events longer than 32 characters. For example, when you try to reload generic_thermostat an event is generated event_generic_thermostat_reloaded which is longer than 32 characters.

I run into this problem also.

Environment: OS/core-2021.3.2

Reloading thermostat entities generates the `event_generic_thermostat_reloaded` event ([see](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/homeassistant/helpers/reload.py#L166)), that is 33 char long, causing nearly the same SQL error.

I suggest to increase the size of `events.event_type` column. Maybe from 32 to 64. The `event_type(32)` is an "ID" similar to `entity_id(255)` but way smaller.

As I see, the next `recorder` version (#47026) will involve some `ALTER TABLE` DB upgrade, maybe this is a good time to modify live DBs!

cc: @bdraco and @CurrentThread from #47026.
That sounds reasonable. I'm happy to review a PR if you want to work one up.
